entry.title: Creating a .NET 10 Application with Clean Architecture: A Practical Multi-Part Guide – Part 7
entry.summary: Part 7 upgrades our Clean Architecture sample with production-grade patterns: FluentValidation for consistent input validation, explicit EF Core transactions for atomic writes, optimistic concurrency using RowVersion, and reliable domain-event publishing via the Outbox pattern. These additions make the system safer under real traffic and failure scenarios, without sacrificing architecture boundaries.

entry.title: Creating a .NET 10 Application with Clean Architecture: A Practical Multi-Part Guide – Part 6
entry.summary: Part 6 adds a real-world read endpoint: fetching a customer’s orders with pagination and sorting. We implement a query use case in the Application layer, a fast EF Core 10 projection in Infrastructure, and expose GET /customers/{id}/orders through Swagger. The result is a scalable, Clean Architecture-friendly read model.

entry.title: Creating a .NET 10 Application with Clean Architecture: A Practical Multi-Part Guide – Part 5
entry.summary: Part 5 expands our Clean Architecture sample by introducing Orders and OrderItems. We model the domain properly, map relationships with EF Core 10, and implement a CreateOrder use case without leaking persistence into the core. Finally, we expose POST /orders in the API and test everything through Swagger.

entry.title: Creating a .NET 10 Application with Clean Architecture: A Practical Multi-Part Guide – Part 4
entry.summary: In Part 4, we replace the in-memory persistence from Part 3 with a real SQL Server database using EF Core 10. We introduce a DbContext, implement repository interfaces, wire dependency injection, and create migrations, without changing domain logic or API endpoints, demonstrating the practical value of Clean Architecture.

entry.title: Creating a .NET 10 Application with Clean Architecture: A Practical Multi-Part Guide – Part 3
entry.summary: In Part 3, we move from setup to real code. We design the first domain entity, implement the CreateCustomer use case in the Application layer, and expose a /customers endpoint through the API. With Swagger enabled, we can already test a complete vertical slicewithout using a database yet.

entry.title: Creating a .NET 10 Application with Clean Architecture: A Practical Multi-Part Guide – Part 2
entry.summary: In Part 2, we prepare the foundation of our application using Visual Studio 2026.
